text:
sara_support: FYI customer PlanitDocs opened an escalation. They started seeing missing instructions and truncated sections after the rollout last night. They say the assistant stopped following the 'Always include section headers' system instruction mid-convo.

olga_support: Ack — do we have a short repro from them? any request/response samples? :thinking_face: 

sara_support: They pasted a redacted convo. Key bits: a 12k-token history, system prompt asking for structured output, then later responses returned as a single paragraph and some sections missing. They also saw a hard cut where the assistant ended with "..." and no closing section.

james_cs: Customer on Hosted API. They upgraded to model variant rwd-3.2 last night during the canary. They say behavior started exactly at deploy time. No auth/billing issues. Latency normal.

tim_engineer: Deploy-bot shows rollout at 2024-11-22T02:12Z to rwd-3.2 for hosted pool A. Canary was 10% traffic -> then ramp. Logging: no obvious 500s. Will check serving config.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout completed for rwd-3.2 -> 100% in hosted pool A at 2024-11-22T03:07Z.

mina_ml: Possible regression in context handling or KV eviction threshold. Did we change max_context_tokens or chunking for rwd-3.2?

tim_engineer: Not in model config, but runtime got a kernel patch that changes how prefix caching is applied for long histories. Patch: "kv-prefetch-adjustment". Shipping note said improved throughput for long sequences.

olga_support: Customer provided API call example. They call completions with conversation history and set max_output_tokens=2048. Here's their simplified request (redacted):

```
POST /v1/completions
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
{
  "model": "rwd-3.2",
  "messages": [ /* ~12k tokens of prior messages */ ],
  "system": "Always include H1/H2 headers and a closing summary.",
  "max_tokens": 2048,
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```

olga_support: Response they got: content truncated mid-section, headers missing in later parts, coherence drops. No 4xx/5xx, HTTP 200.

mina_ml: Can they share a redacted transcript and the exact returned token count? Also need top-level routing headers (X-Request-ID, X-Model-Variant) from response.

sara_support: Requested transcript + request/response headers. They already sent the X-Request-IDs for three failing calls: req-6a1b, req-6a2c, req-6b0f.

sre-oncall: Looking at logs for those request ids now. Seeing normal tail latency. Interesting: runtime shows early KV eviction events around the same timestamps (evict=prefix, reason=age_limit).

tim_engineer: That lines up with the kernel patch — we lowered the per-segment retention when memory pressure hit a threshold. Might be too aggressive. If KV cache evicts important system prompt state, output can lose structure.

mina_ml: Hypothesis: eviction incorrectly considers system tokens as non-pinned when prefix-cache compaction runs. Need to reproduce locally using same model binary and runtime flags.

olga_support: Customer expects a fix ASAP. They’re on PROD and have live users. CS requests prioritization.

tim_engineer: Action items: 1) recreate on staging with rwd-3.2 + same runtime kernel patch and a 12k token history; 2) run with kv-prefetch-adjustment off/old behavior; 3) collect token-level KV usage traces and model logits for the segment where headers drop.

mina_ml: I'll set up a reproducer. Can someone drop the exact conversation sample (redacted) into the secure reproducible bucket? Preferably truncated to the minimal example that triggers the loss.

sara_support: Uploaded the redacted transcript to s3://redwood-support-repro/planitdocs/1845129034/redacted.txt and added the three request ids to the ticket. Giving devs access now.

tim_engineer: Thx. Also can we check routing fallback? If requests were routed to a quantized fallback variant with a different context policy that could explain truncation.

sre-oncall: Checked routing logs: all three req-ids stuck to rwd-3.2-hosted-A, no fallback.

mina_ml: Reproducer in progress. Quick test locally: I simulated a 12k history + system instruction and toggled eviction threshold. With the relaxed retention (current patch) I see header tokens evicted around step ~345 and outputs lose the H2 sections. With old retention they remain.

tim_engineer: Good find. We should hotfix runtime to revert the kv-prefetch-adjustment on hosted pool A and roll back to prior retention policy while we investigate.

olga_support: CS confirmed PlanitDocs is okay with a rollback as mitigation, they just need stability. 

deploy-bot: Rolling back kernel patch on hosted pool A to previous runtime build at 2024-11-22T04:30Z (initiated).

sre-oncall: Monitoring rollback. Will update when Canary back to prior binary.

sara_support: Customer notified of mitigation plan and ETA ~20min. They asked for post-mortem and steps we’ll take to prevent recurrence.

mina_ml: Follow-ups: add an automated regression test that runs long-history structured-prompt evaluations on canary after any kernel change; track metrics: fraction of responses missing expected anchor tokens (e.g., H1/H2 markers) over test prompts.

tim_engineer: Agree. Also add an observability metric: KV eviction of system/pinned token count per request and alert if >0 for requests with system instructions.

james_cs: Noted for the customer post-mortem. Will send a one-pager explaining cause, mitigation (rollback), timeline, and prevention steps.

olga_support: Customer confirmed behavior improved after rollback (initial checks). They'll run their acceptance test and report back. :relieved: 

sara_support: Closing loop once they confirm. Thanks team.

mina_ml: I'll follow up with a more detailed repro report and a patch to mark system tokens as pinned in prefix compaction.

tim_engineer: Assigning issue to ENG-7894 (kv-eviction-system-pins).

sre-oncall: Canary completed rollback at 2024-11-22T04:45Z. No further eviction events for the recent request ids.

olga_support: PlanitDocs acceptance passed for sample cases. They're monitoring production. 

sara_support: Marking as escalated -> resolved for now. Will reopen if customer sees reoccurrence. :white_check_mark:
